mode: Original Queue WebView login retained; no separate Chrome/CDP to the user's Chrome, no shop-tab architecture change
observedProblem: Roblox kept answering the customer sign-in with the 'Verify you're human / Press and hold' card.
causes: The form was filled by assigning input.value from script and submitted with element.click(), so every event was untrusted and the submit followed instantly, which is the pattern automated clients produce.
Each attempt used a brand-new browser profile, so the device looked new every time (fixed in 1.3.3).
changes: Both fields are typed with DevTools protocol key events (isTrusted) at 28-72ms per character instead of a scripted value assignment; the checked scripted fill remains as a fallback when focusing or typing fails.
The sign-in button is clicked with real mouse events at its on-screen position after scrolling it into view.
New offline harness tests/native/InputProbe.cs proves the fixture page receives only trusted events, that the values match, and that a trusted click submits once.
The same harness has a live mode that signs in with a random nonexistent username to prove the real page accepts typed input and reaches its own error message without a challenge.
nativeBuild: passed x64 compile and full native self-tests
nativeInputTests: INPUT_OK offline: 30 trusted key events, 0 untrusted, trusted click, one submit, exact values

livePublicProbe.result: LIVE_INPUT_OK: both fields typed, trusted click, page answered 'Incorrect username or password.' (CUSTOMER_PASSWORD_INVALID), challengeVisible=false
livePublicProbe.stored: no credentials written to disk; probe profile deleted

installation: Staged 1.3.5 in LOCALAPPDATA and D:\BewpakornQueue-1.0.0\extension; release checksums, live extension hashes and installed host hash verified.
preservedData: Ledger and history untouched; the blocked order becomes retryable when the new host starts.
limitations: No real customer account was used, so whether Roblox still challenges a specific account cannot be proven here.
A challenge, if Roblox decides on one, still needs a single human press; the host then continues and finishes the form by itself.
